completedTasks.title: OTLP export: review, owner gates, and the fixes
completedTasks.summary: Reviewed the OTLP export surface against the OTLP spec, the OTel semantic conventions and the decompiled opentelemetry-dotnet 1.17.0 assemblies, then fixed everything two owner gates approved (18/18, then 9/9). Defects: promotion-queue instruments modelled SQLite-persisted state with process-lifetime deltas (depth could read negative after a restart); the bare-launch host never disposed, and provider disposal is the SDK's only flush trigger; a scheme-less OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT threw out of StartAsync and killed the server, while localhost:4318 parsed with Scheme=localhost and failed silently; every exported span carried a dangling parent_span_id; the signal path doubled on trailing-slash and case-varied endpoints; quiet mode kept a stderr provider and leaked Warning+ into the channel Hermes owns. Conventions: one derived OtlpNames registry with a guard that fails on an unregistered meter, dotted names with units, duration moved to mcp.server.operation.duration in seconds, MCP semconv on the span (mcp.method.name, gen_ai.tool.name, error.type, AddException), service.version, System.Net.Http, and the promotion tags. Structure: D1 replaced 22 hand-repeated instrumentation call sites with a single CallToolFilter — which revealed that 21 of 22 tools emitted NOTHING for marshaller-rejected calls, a class of call per-method instrumentation structurally cannot reach; and WP13 instrumented the four background services through a Core port, closing the last dark surface. WP7 exported the ASP.NET request span (ADR-0021, reversing a standing non-goal on owner ruling) and then removed the AlwaysOnSampler, restoring OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER after it had been inert since 2026-08-08 — held until the proxy lane's ForwardedRequests_CarryNoTraceparent proved on the wire that nothing propagates traceparent, since otherwise removal would have silently dropped every server span. Also fixed two CI flakes: a zero-byte download treated as success in three places INCLUDING the production fresh-install path (the SHA gate was hashing nothing), and made the native SIGSEGV diagnosable — its mechanism was established at register level (GC mark phase, #GP on a non-canonical pointer read from a corrupted object header) but the corrupting component was not, and no test was invented for it. Corrected ADR-0002 (now Superseded) and ADR-0009's four false claims, closed the documentation drift including SECURITY.md's privacy table citing a deleted method, and fed the root cause of a worktree collision back to ai-badger as 0.115.1.

completedTasks.title: Fix every issue found in the 1.5.0 manual testing sweep
completedTasks.summary: Reviewed the sweep findings against the code before planning, which upgraded the headline defect: PromoteAsync dequeued each candidate before sharing it (separate connections, no transaction, no try/catch), so a queued hash whose entry had been re-ingested was PERMANENTLY LOST, not merely mis-reported. Root cause: nothing invalidated promotion_queue when the entries rows it referenced were deleted or re-chunked - asserted as intended in a then-green test (Sweep_NeverTouchesTheQueue). Live: 19 orphaned rows, ai-raccoon's rank-1 candidate among them, so every 30-minute pass destroyed the top candidate and promoted nothing. Fixes (#232): AFTER DELETE ON entries trigger with a NOT EXISTS sibling guard (additive DDL, no schema-version bump) + ai-raccoon extract prune; per-candidate isolation in PromoteAsync with PromoteOutcome.Failures and ShareExtractResult.{SkippedDuplicates,Failures}; typed invalid-argument refusals across all 22 tools; foreign-subject detector no longer fires on ids inside brackets, many-foreign-projects tag split out, mid-sentence channel boundary pinned by tests; ADR-0023 and ADR-0024; sweep-doc and reference corrections; 1.6.0 bump and a README 'What's new (from 1.2.0 to 1.6.0)' section. NO scoring weight, prior or clamp changed - the calibration fixture (AIRACCOON_SCORING_EVAL_FIXTURE) is deliberately uncommitted, so a weight change is unmeasurable; gated on committing a labeled fixture. The quality gate then found two defects the packages' own tests missed, fixed in #237: extract prune crashed on every invocation (GetValue read 'apply' for an option declared '--apply'; the store-level test never touched argv), and the new trigger destroyed candidates for UNCHANGED chunks on a watched-file re-ingest (content-derived hashes return identical, but nothing backs them at delete time) - now handled by capturing and restoring the affected queue rows across ReplaceFileAsync's transaction. Refusals also narrowed to exact types so ArgumentOutOfRangeException (our own index bugs) is not laundered into a caller-facing invalid-argument at Information level. Live restore run with a locally built 1.6.0: 30 orphans -> 0, prune idempotent, queue 970. Extraction deliberately left on 'propose' - the background service runs inside the installed 1.5.0 backend, so flipping to 'promote' would still execute the old dequeue-before-share code. Next: tag/publish 1.6.0, dotnet tool update, serve --restart, then flip extract.mode.global back to promote.

completedTasks.title: Direct-HTTP clients can present the loopback token again
completedTasks.summary: ADR-0020's token gate left every non-proxy route unable to authenticate; the Hermes plugin's http transport was one of four surfaces, not the defect. The gate now also accepts Authorization: Bearer (one credential, two envelopes, FixedTimeEquals on both) because `hermes mcp add --url` prompts for authentication by default and can only produce Bearer. serve --mcp-entry prints a headers map with a ${AIRACCOON_MCP_TOKEN} placeholder instead of a bare URL - verified against the installed CLIs that both Hermes and Claude Code expand it, and that an unset variable warns but still sends the literal string, which is why /mcp now renders a distinct 401 for a present-but-wrong credential (an unexpanded placeholder is a present one; the old wording told users to add the header they had just added). The plugin reads token_file, default ~/.ai-raccoon/mcp-token, and attaches it only for loopback URLs. Pre-implementation review caught that the naive default would have shipped the loopback secret to whatever url was configured, and that one 'seen RED' recipe could not fire on any machine that had run ai-raccoon. Post-implementation review caught follow_redirects=True keeping a custom header across origins - a token-exfiltration path the plan's own residual-risk paragraph had reasoned away on a premise a different lane invalidated. QA against a real gated server found the client discarding the server's diagnostic entirely: anyio surfaced the 401 as asyncio.CancelledError, a BaseException with an empty str(), outside the except Exception in both connect() and the provider. 1.6.0.
decisions: ADR-0020:182 asserted `serve --mcp-entry` was unaffected and a direct url entry remained valid. False the day it was written - the token shipped in the same change. That assertion is why nobody re-checked the direct route. Struck and marked as corrected rather than reworded.

The mismatch 401 is scoped to /mcp. ADR-0022 guards /shutdown with the same gate and pins one identical body for absent/wrong/truncated so the refusal cannot say whether a token exists - a tested invariant, not a comment. /mcp is configured by hand and needs the diagnosability; /shutdown's only caller is `serve --restart` reading the token off disk and gains nothing from it.

No WWW-Authenticate on the 401 despite accepting a Bearer envelope. RFC 7235 makes it a MUST, but a bare Bearer challenge may push spec-following clients into an OAuth discovery flow this server does not serve. Recorded as a considered trade-off.

completedTasks.title: Unwrap the ApiEnvelope in the Hermes provider client
completedTasks.pr: 171 (squash-merged as a913c93; #170 closed - it was branched off unpushed local commits and inherited an unrelated red build)
completedTasks.summary: Every MCP tool answers ApiEnvelope<T> = {data, meta} but the Hermes provider client returned it verbatim, so __init__.py:262 read payload.get('results') off the wrapper: Hermes prefetch had been silently returning zero memories against any current server - no exception, no log line, just an empty '## AiRaccoon Memory' block every turn. Fix is one seam: client.py _call now returns _unwrap(_text(result)); _unwrap requires BOTH envelope keys so a payload carrying its own 'data' field survives, and the isError path keeps raw text because errors travel the McpException channel. Ruled out as a rename regression by running the same 5 integration tests at pre-rename 74bb2e1 and seeing them fail identically. completedTasks.title: Post-MoE integration review: 7-lane audit of everything since v1.1.2, 10 blockers fixed, release 1.2.0
completedTasks.summary: Seven Opus review lanes over ~20 PRs merged since v1.1.2 (tools/ToolGate, extraction+promotion, observability, HKDF crypto, watch, architecture, docs/CI/release). Ten blockers found and fixed; ~20 Medium/Low filed as #115-#121. CRITICAL, shipped alone as #114 so it stays revertable: #88's settings strip protected only the FIRST push -- when a remote object existed, the merge branch re-VACUUMed the live bank into mergedPath and pushed it unstripped, and the conflict-retry path did the same, so every push after the first uploaded S3/Azure credentials and embedding.apiKey into the bucket those credentials unlock. Existing tests missed it because the settings test seeded an EMPTY cloud store (only the remote-is-null branch ran) and the merge test asserted the LOCAL bank, never the pushed payload. RED verified by reverting the production file and watching both new tests fail on the settings count. #125 carried the rest: (1) OTLP -- Sources.Clear() emptied the IConfiguration the OTel SDK binds OTEL_* from, so only four hand-parsed vars worked; measured on the wire that HEADERS, RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES and COMPRESSION never reached it, meaning any authenticated collector 401'd silently while the CLI said 'enabled'; fixed by re-admitting only OTEL_-prefixed keys. I overrode the implementing agent here: it hardcoded service.name, removing OTEL_SERVICE_NAME, which had been one of the few working vars -- owner confirmed keeping the override. (2) remove-then-re-add ran NO catch-up scan and the integration test pinning it could not fail (RemoveAsync never deletes entries, so its >= assertion held before any work). (3) shutdown never cancelled an in-flight scan; CancelAllScans had no production caller at all. (4) a candidate the agent explicitly discarded could still be shared, irreversibly (no unshare API) -- fixed with DELETE...RETURNING claim-then-share. (5) ai_raccoon_queue_discarded_total would have shipped reading permanent zero beside the brand-new OTLP export. (6) a healthy bank reported 'corrupt... restore from a backup' whenever any post-open SqliteException occurred (e.g. the MCP server holding the bank); the migrate verb had the identical bug. Docs: the nuget.org README advertised 20 tools (there are 22) -- now gated by a test; the HKDF rekey (#99: 20 files, zero docs) documented with a how-to; the reference doc had still described the SUPERSEDED derivation ADR 0012 exists to eliminate; SECURITY.md claimed no releases (14 exist) and no CI (4 workflows). PASSED CLEAN, worth not re-deriving: HKDF is genuine RFC 5869 via platform HKDF.DeriveKey (re-verified against an independent implementation, both pinned vectors match); the rekey gate cannot lose data; all EventIds unique; Core's layering is compiler-enforced; #97/#110/#111 genuinely de-duplicated without leaving competing mechanisms. MACHINE FINDING, corrects a standing belief: the build wedges are NOT node reuse. 31 'aspire nuget search' processes from a DIFFERENT repo (job-search-ai-assistant), oldest 2h06m, held the NuGet lock; restore sat 19m23s and completed within seconds of killing them. Directory.Build.rsp's -nodeReuse:false works but records the wrong cause, and the MSBuild processes 'wedged' 3-7h were Rider restores starved on the same lock. PROCESS: main moved FIVE times mid-task (#111 -> #112 -> #113 -> #114 -> #122 -> #123/#124); re-verified against each new head rather than trusting earlier reads, which is how #123 closing WI-6a was caught before shipping a stale plan. The MoE plan doc was reconciled against code: its still-open list named five already-shipped items and WI-7c/WI-7e had fallen off the document entirely. completedTasks.title: Watch catch-up runaway: removal now stops the scan, and only one process scans a watch
completedTasks.summary: Incident: a watch registered under the wrong project id, removed mid-scan, kept re-chunking docs (~5,600 duplicate entries, 100-150% CPU); a direct SQLite DELETE could not stop it and only pkill of the stdio servers did. Three verified defects. (1) WatchHostedService.ReconcileAsync's stale sweep stopped the event source but never called WatchPipeline.UnregisterWatch, whose only caller was WatchService.RemoveAsync - so any out-of-band removal left the pipeline resolving that path for the process's life; the sweep also iterated _active, which holds only enabled watches, so a disabled project's registration could never be swept (#93). (2) The catch-up scan took no CancellationToken at all - ReconcileAsync had the host token in scope and dropped it, StopAsync never touched it - so a scan survived both removal and shutdown; fixed with WatchScanGuard single-flight plus cancellation hung off UnregisterWatch as one choke point (#95). (3) Nothing coordinated the ~31 concurrent stdio servers on one bank; SqliteWatchScanLease now holds a TTL lease on the watches row, owner id machine:pid:guid, crash recovery by expiry alone (#101). Wiring it surfaced a fourth defect the plan had specified and the implementation dropped: ScanCoreAsync acquired and released but never renewed, so a scan outliving the 60s TTL lost its lease and kept enqueueing - renewal now runs inline before each enqueue. Removal also cascades watch_files fingerprints via a constant that existed and was wired to nothing (#94). The open assumption is closed: RemoveThenReAdd_ReIngestsEveryFile_WithoutDuplicateEntries passes, so entry-level dedup was never broken - the duplicates came from repeated full-tree scans (#104). Also committed the 23MB bundled ONNX model instead of gitignoring it, after a fresh worktree cost 48 spurious test failures (#98), and added Directory.Build.rsp with -nodeReuse:false after 11 dotnet build processes deadlocked on MSBuild node reuse, the oldest blocked 3.5 hours (2ccd848).

Dapper 2.1.79 parameter binding is case-sensitive against SQL param names and its record ctor matching chokes on nullable params — alias columns and use a settable DTO
sqlite-memory/vector/sync are native SQLite extensions loaded via Microsoft.Data.Sqlite LoadExtension; deferred embeddings (defer_embeddings=1) let writes work before any model is configured
MCP protocol CallToolResult.IsError is null on success (absent), true only on failure — assert ShouldNotBe(true), not ShouldBe(false)
Bare `ai-raccoon` is a proxy: it opens no bank, resolves no key and loads no ONNX model. `--transport stdio` is the in-process server and the escape hatch when a backend cannot start

`serve` mints <data-root>/mcp-token (0600) BEFORE it binds, so a port that answers guarantees the file exists; the probe accepts 401 as proof of a live server so it still recognises one across data roots

/mcp and /shutdown accept the loopback token in either envelope: X-AiRaccoon-Token or Authorization: Bearer <token>, one credential compared with FixedTimeEquals on both paths and neither shadowing the other. /mcp alone renders a second 401 body for a credential that was presented but did not match; /shutdown keeps one body for every failure because ADR-0022 pins the refusal not to reveal whether a token exists. `serve --mcp-entry` prints a headers map carrying ${AIRACCOON_MCP_TOKEN}, never a live token - Hermes resolves it from ~/.hermes/.env, Claude Code from the environment, and an unset variable in Claude Code warns in `claude mcp list` but still sends the literal placeholder.
